body.en: Advanced ACT Math requires fluency across multi-variable linear and non-linear systems, matrix algebraic structures, polynomial factor theorems, and logarithmic equations requiring extraneous root verification.
body.ar: Advanced ACT Math requires fluency across multi-المتغير linear and non-linear systems, المصفوفة algebraic structures, كثيرة الحدود factor theorems, and logarithmic المعادلات requiring extraneous root verification.

label.en: Definition 2.1 — Matrix Arithmetic, Determinants, and Inverses
label.ar: تعريف 2.1 — المصفوفة Arithmetic, Determinants, and Inverses

body.en:
Matrix conventions for standardized mathematics examinations:
  • Matrix Addition and Scalar Multiplication: Defined entrywise for matrices of identical dimensions \(m \times n\).
  • Matrix Product (\(AB\)): The product \(A_{m \times k} B_{k \times n}\) produces an \(m \times n\) matrix where entry \((i, j)\) is the dot product of row \(i\) of \(A\) and column \(j\) of \(B\). Matrix multiplication is non-commutative: \(AB \neq BA\) in general.
  • \(2 \times 2\) Determinant & Inverse: For \(A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\):
    \[ \det(A) = |A| = ad - bc \]\[ A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix} \quad (\text{provided } \det(A) \neq 0) \]
  • Multiplicative Determinant Property: For square matrices \(A\) and \(B\), \(\det(AB) = \det(A) \cdot \det(B)\).
body.ar:
المصفوفة conventions for standardized mathematics examinations:
  • Matrix Addition and Scalar Multiplication: Defined entrywise for المصفوفات of identical dimensions \(m \times n\).
  • Matrix Product (\(AB\)): The product \(A_{m \times k} B_{k \times n}\) produces an \(m \times n\) المصفوفة حيث entry \((i, j)\) is the dot product of row \(i\) of \(A\) and column \(j\) of \(B\). المصفوفة multiplication is non-commutative: \(AB \neq BA\) in general.
  • \(2 \times 2\) المحدد & Inverse: For \(A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\):
    \[ \det(A) = |A| = ad - bc \]\[ A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix} \quad (\text{provided } \det(A) \neq 0) \]
  • Multiplicative المحدد Property: For square المصفوفات \(A\) and \(B\), \(\det(AB) = \det(A) \cdot \det(B)\).

label.ar: ● الحدس المفاهيمي العميق — Advanced الجبر & Systems

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across ACT International Subject Test — Math 1, multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.
body.ar: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across ACT International Subject Test — Math 1, multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—الثابت rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-المتغير linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique التقاطع if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no الحل (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many الحلول if all three ratios coincide.

label.en: Theorem 2.1 — Polynomial Theorems and Logarithmic Properties
label.ar: مبرهنة 2.1 — كثيرة الحدود Theorems and Logarithmic Properties

body.en:
High-rigor algebraic principles:
  • Polynomial Remainder & Factor Theorems: When a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - c\), the remainder is \(R = P(c)\). Consequently, \((x - c)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) if and only if \(P(c) = 0\).
  • Rational Root Theorem: Any rational root of \(a_n x^n + \dots + a_1 x + a_0 = 0\) with integer coefficients has the form \(\pm \frac{p}{q}\), where \(p\) divides \(a_0\) and \(q\) divides \(a_n\).
  • Logarithm Laws:
    \[ \log_b(xy) = \log_b x + \log_b y, \quad \log_b(x/y) = \log_b x - \log_b y, \quad \log_b(x^k) = k\log_b x \]
  • Extraneous Root Principle: Because \(\log_b(u)\) requires \(u > 0\) and \(\sqrt{u}\) requires \(u \ge 0\), solving converted polynomial forms may introduce extraneous roots that must be checked against the original expressions.
body.ar:

  • Rational Root مبرهنة: Any rational root of \(a_n x^n + \dots + a_1 x + a_0 = 0\) with integer المعاملات has the form \(\pm \frac{p}{q}\), حيث \(p\) divides \(a_0\) and \(q\) divides \(a_n\).
  • Logarithm Laws:

  • Extraneous Root Principle: Because \(\log_b(u)\) requires \(u > 0\) and \(\sqrt{u}\) requires \(u \ge 0\), solving converted كثيرة الحدود forms may introduce extraneous roots that must be checked against the original expressions.

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Matrices & Advanced Systems
label.ar: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — المصفوفات & Advanced Systems

body.en:
• Matrix Multiplication Order & Dimensions: To compute \(AB\), the number of columns in \(A\) (inner dimension) must equal the number of rows in \(B\): \((m imes k) imes (k imes n) = (m imes n)\). Furthermore, \(AB eq BA\) in general — matrix multiplication is non-commutative!
  • Determinant & Singularity: For \(A = egin{pmatrix} a & b \ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), \(\det(A) = ad - bc\). The matrix inverse \(A^{-1}\) exists if and only if \(\det(A) eq 0\). If \(\det(A) = 0\), the corresponding linear system has either no unique solution (inconsistent or dependent).
  • Extraneous Solutions in Rational Equations: When clearing denominators by multiplying by a common multiple, values that make any original denominator equal to zero are extraneous and must be discarded.
  • Logarithm Bases & Power Properties: Remember \(\log_b(A + B) eq \log_b A + \log_b B\). The addition rule applies only inside the logarithm: \(\log_b(AB) = \log_b A + \log_b B\).
body.ar:

  • Determinant & Singularity: For \(A = egin{pmatrix} a & b \ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), \(\det(A) = ad - bc\). The المصفوفة inverse \(A^{-1}\) exists if and only if \(\det(A) eq 0\). If \(\det(A) = 0\), the corresponding linear system has either no unique الحل (inconsistent or dependent).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Advanced Algebra & Systems)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Advanced الجبر & Systems)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

body.en:
Find all intersection points of the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 25\) and the line \(x - y = 1\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Isolate \(x\) in the linear equation: \(x = y + 1\).
  2. Substitute into the circle equation:
    \[ (y + 1)^2 + y^2 = 25 \implies (y^2 + 2y + 1) + y^2 = 25 \]\[ 2y^2 + 2y - 24 = 0 \implies y^2 + y - 12 = 0 \]
  3. Factor the quadratic:
    \[ (y + 4)(y - 3) = 0 \implies y = 3 \quad \text{or} \quad y = -4 \]
  4. Determine corresponding \(x\)-values using \(x = y + 1\):
    If \(y = 3\): \(x = 3 + 1 = 4\), yielding \((4, 3)\).
    If \(y = -4\): \(x = -4 + 1 = -3\), yielding \((-3, -4)\).
  5. Verify in both equations:
    \(4^2 + 3^2 = 16 + 9 = 25\) and \(4 - 3 = 1\).
    \((-3)^2 + (-4)^2 = 9 + 16 = 25\) and \(-3 - (-4) = 1\).
The two intersection points are \(\mathbf{(4, 3)}\) and \(\mathbf{(-3, -4)}\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.B — Solving a Logarithmic Equation with Extraneous Roots
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.B — Solving a Logarithmic المعادلة with Extraneous Roots

body.en:
Solve the equation \(\log_2(x + 3) + \log_2(x - 1) = 5\) for real \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Combine terms using the product rule \(\log_b A + \log_b B = \log_b(AB)\):
    \[ \log_2[(x + 3)(x - 1)] = 5 \]
  2. Convert to exponential form:
    \[ (x + 3)(x - 1) = 2^5 = 32 \]
  3. Expand and set to zero:
    \[ x^2 + 2x - 3 = 32 \implies x^2 + 2x - 35 = 0 \]
  4. Factor the quadratic:
    \[ (x + 7)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -7 \]
  5. Verify against domain restrictions (\(x + 3 > 0 \implies x > -3\) and \(x - 1 > 0 \implies x > 1\)):
    For \(x = -7\): \(\log_2(-4)\) is undefined in real numbers (extraneous).
    For \(x = 5\): \(\log_2(8) + \log_2(4) = 3 + 2 = 5\) (valid).
The unique real solution is \(\mathbf{x = 5}\).

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — Advanced Algebra & Systems (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(C\) — Advanced الجبر & Systems (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): In the standard \((x, y)\) coordinate plane, the system of equations \[ \begin{cases} y = |x^2 - 4| \\ y = 2x + k \end{cases} \] has exactly 3 distinct real solutions \((x, y)\). What is the sum of all possible values of the real constant \(k\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: The system represents the intersections of the absolute-value quadratic graph \( y = |x^2 - 4| \) and the family of parallel lines \( y = 2x + k \) of slope 2. The piecewise definition of \( y = |x^2 - 4| \) is: \[ y = \begin{cases} x^2 - 4, & \text{if } |x| \ge 2 \\ 4 - x^2, & \text{if } |x| < 2 \end{cases} \] To find when there are exactly 3 intersection points, analyze the critical transitions as \( k \) increases: 1. **Tangency to the inverted arch \( y = 4 - x^2 \)**: Setting the derivative equal to the slope of the line: \[ \frac{d}{dx}(4 - x^2) = -2x = 2 \implies x = -1 \] At \( x = -1 \), \( y = 4 - (-1)^2 = 3 \). Substituting \((-1, 3)\) into the line equation: \[ 3 = 2(-1) + k \implies k = 5 \] For \( k = 5 \), the line is tangent to the inverted portion at \( x = -1 \) (1 solution) and intersects the outer branches \( x^2 - 4 = 2x + 5 \implies x^2 - 2x - 9 = 0 \implies x = 1 \pm \sqrt{10} \). Since \( 1 + \sqrt{10} > 2 \) and \( 1 - \sqrt{10} < -2 \), these give 2 additional real solutions, totaling exactly **3 distinct solutions**. 2. **Passing through the left vertex/cusp \((-2, 0)\)**: Substitute \((-2, 0)\) into the line equation: \[ 0 = 2(-2) + k \implies k = 4 \] For \( k = 4 \), the line \( y = 2x + 4 \) intersects: - The inverted arch \( 4 - x^2 = 2x + 4 \implies x^2 + 2x = 0 \implies x = 0 \) and \( x = -2 \). - The right outer branch \( x^2 - 4 = 2x + 4 \implies x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0 \implies (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0 \implies x = 4 \). Thus, the solutions are \( x \in \{-2, 0, 4\} \), which gives exactly **3 distinct solutions**. 3. **Behavior in other intervals of \( k \)**: - For \( k > 5 \): 2 solutions (outer branches only). - For \( 4 < k < 5 \): 4 solutions (2 on the inverted arch, 2 on the outer branches). - For \( -4 < k < 4 \): 2 solutions. - For \( k = -4 \): 1 solution (passing through \((2, 0)\)). - For \( k < -4 \): 0 solutions. Therefore, the only values of \( k \) that yield exactly 3 distinct solutions are \( k = 4 \) and \( k = 5 \). Their sum is \( 4 + 5 = 9 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): In the standard \((x, y)\) الإحداثي plane, the system of المعادلات \[ \begin{cases} y = |x^2 - 4| \\ y = 2x + k \end{cases} \] has exactly 3 distinct real الحلول \((x, y)\). What is the sum of all possible values of the real الثابت \(k\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: The system represents the intersections of the absolute-value quadratic التمثيل البياني \( y = |x^2 - 4| \) and the family of parallel lines \( y = 2x + k \) of الميل 2. The piecewise definition of \( y = |x^2 - 4| \) is: \[ y = \begin{cases} x^2 - 4, & \text{if } |x| \ge 2 \\ 4 - x^2, & \text{if } |x| < 2 \end{cases} \] To find عندما there are exactly 3 التقاطع points, analyze the critical transitions as \( k \) increases: 1. **Tangency to the inverted arch \( y = 4 - x^2 \)**: Setting the المشتقة equal to the الميل of the line: \[ \frac{d}{dx}(4 - x^2) = -2x = 2 \implies x = -1 \] At \( x = -1 \), \( y = 4 - (-1)^2 = 3 \). Substituting \((-1, 3)\) into the line المعادلة: \[ 3 = 2(-1) + k \implies k = 5 \] For \( k = 5 \), the line is tangent to the inverted portion at \( x = -1 \) (1 الحل) and intersects the outer branches \( x^2 - 4 = 2x + 5 \implies x^2 - 2x - 9 = 0 \implies x = 1 \pm \sqrt{10} \). Since \( 1 + \sqrt{10} > 2 \) and \( 1 - \sqrt{10} < -2 \), these give 2 additional real الحلول, totaling exactly **3 distinct الحلول**. 2. **Passing through the left الرأس/cusp \((-2, 0)\)**: عوّض \((-2, 0)\) into the line المعادلة: \[ 0 = 2(-2) + k \implies k = 4 \] For \( k = 4 \), the line \( y = 2x + 4 \) intersects: - The inverted arch \( 4 - x^2 = 2x + 4 \implies x^2 + 2x = 0 \implies x = 0 \) and \( x = -2 \). - The right outer branch \( x^2 - 4 = 2x + 4 \implies x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0 \implies (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0 \implies x = 4 \). وعليه, the الحلول are \( x \in \{-2, 0, 4\} \), which gives exactly **3 distinct الحلول**. 3. **Behavior in other intervals of \( k \)**: - For \( k > 5 \): 2 الحلول (outer branches only). - For \( 4 < k < 5 \): 4 الحلول (2 on the inverted arch, 2 on the outer branches). - For \( -4 < k < 4 \): 2 الحلول. - For \( k = -4 \): 1 الحل (passing through \((2, 0)\)). - For \( k < -4 \): 0 الحلول. وبالتالي, the only values of \( k \) that yield exactly 3 distinct الحلول are \( k = 4 \) and \( k = 5 \). Their sum is \( 4 + 5 = 9 \).

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Advanced Algebra & Systems (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — Advanced الجبر & Systems (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Consider the system of linear equations below: \[ \begin{cases} 3x - 2y = 8 \\ kx + 6y = 5 \end{cases} \] For which of the following values of the constant \( k \) does the system have no solution \((x, y)\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: A system of two linear equations in two variables has no solution if and only if the lines represented by the equations are parallel and distinct (they have the same slope but different \( y \)-intercepts). First, rewrite each equation in slope-intercept form \( y = mx + b \): 1. For the first equation: \[ 3x - 2y = 8 \implies -2y = -3x + 8 \implies y = \frac{3}{2}x - 4 \] The slope of the first line is \( m_1 = \frac{3}{2} \) and the \( y \)-intercept is \( -4 \). 2. For the second equation: \[ kx + 6y = 5 \implies 6y = -kx + 5 \implies y = -\frac{k}{6}x + \frac{5}{6} \] The slope of the second line is \( m_2 = -\frac{k}{6} \) and the \( y \)-intercept is \( \frac{5}{6} \). Since the \( y \)-intercepts \( -4 \) and \( \frac{5}{6} \) are unequal, the lines will be distinct and parallel whenever their slopes are equal: \[ \frac{3}{2} = -\frac{k}{6} \] Cross-multiplying yields: \[ 2(-k) = 3(6) \implies -2k = 18 \implies k = -9 \] Alternatively, using the coefficient determinant criterion for parallelism: \[ \det \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ k & 6 \end{pmatrix} = 3(6) - (-2)(k) = 18 + 2k = 0 \implies k = -9 \] Common Misconceptions: - Choosing \( 9 \): Results from a sign error when isolating \( y \) or evaluating the determinant \( 18 - 2k = 0 \). - Choosing \( -4 \) or \( 4 \): Results from incorrectly combining coefficients column-wise (e.g., \( 3k + 12 = 0 \)) rather than cross-multiplying.
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): Consider the system of المعادلات الخطية below: \[ \begin{cases} 3x - 2y = 8 \\ kx + 6y = 5 \end{cases} \] For which of the following values of the الثابت \( k \) does the system have no الحل \((x, y)\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: A system of two المعادلات الخطية in two المتغيرات has no الحل if and only if the lines represented by the المعادلات are parallel and distinct (they have the same الميل but different \( y \)-intercepts). First, rewrite each المعادلة in الميل-المقطع form \( y = mx + b \): 1. For the first المعادلة: \[ 3x - 2y = 8 \implies -2y = -3x + 8 \implies y = \frac{3}{2}x - 4 \] The الميل of the first line is \( m_1 = \frac{3}{2} \) and the \( y \)-المقطع is \( -4 \). 2. For the second المعادلة: \[ kx + 6y = 5 \implies 6y = -kx + 5 \implies y = -\frac{k}{6}x + \frac{5}{6} \] The الميل of the second line is \( m_2 = -\frac{k}{6} \) and the \( y \)-المقطع is \( \frac{5}{6} \). Since the \( y \)-intercepts \( -4 \) and \( \frac{5}{6} \) are unequal, the lines will be distinct and parallel whenever their slopes are equal: \[ \frac{3}{2} = -\frac{k}{6} \] Cross-multiplying yields: \[ 2(-k) = 3(6) \implies -2k = 18 \implies k = -9 \] Alternatively, using the المعامل المحدد criterion for parallelism: \[ \det \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ k & 6 \end{pmatrix} = 3(6) - (-2)(k) = 18 + 2k = 0 \implies k = -9 \] Common Misconceptions: - Choosing \( 9 \): Results from a sign error عندما isolating \( y \) or evaluating the المحدد \( 18 - 2k = 0 \). - Choosing \( -4 \) or \( 4 \): Results from incorrectly combining المعاملات column-wise (e.g., \( 3k + 12 = 0 \)) rather than cross-multiplying.

question.en: Solve for \(x\): \(3^{x+1} = 5^x\). Express your solution in terms of natural logarithms.
question.ar: أوجد قيمة \(x\): \(3^{x+1} = 5^x\). Express your solution in terms of natural logarithms.

solution.en:
Take the natural logarithm \(\ln\) of both sides:
\[ \ln(3^{x+1}) = \ln(5^x) \implies (x + 1)\ln 3 = x\ln 5 \]\[ x\ln 3 + \ln 3 = x\ln 5 \implies \ln 3 = x\ln 5 - x\ln 3 = x(\ln 5 - \ln 3) \]\[ x = \frac{\ln 3}{\ln 5 - \ln 3} = \mathbf{\frac{\ln 3}{\ln(5/3)}} \approx 2.151 \]
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية: Take the natural logarithm \(\ln\) of both sides:
\[ \ln(3^{x+1}) = \ln(5^x) \implies (x + 1)\ln 3 = x\ln 5 \]\[ x\ln 3 + \ln 3 = x\ln 5 \implies \ln 3 = x\ln 5 - x\ln 3 = x(\ln 5 - \ln 3) \]\[ x = \frac{\ln 3}{\ln 5 - \ln 3} = \mathbf{\frac{\ln 3}{\ln(5/3)}} \approx 2.151 \]

question.en: Let matrices \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\). Compute \(AB\), \(\det(A)\), \(\det(B)\), and verify that \(\det(AB) = \det(A)\det(B)\).
question.ar: ليكن matrices \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\). Compute \(AB\), \(\det(A)\), \(\det(B)\), and verإذا كانy that \(\det(AB) = \det(A)\det(B)\).

solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية:

(a) Product \(AB\):
\[ AB = \begin{pmatrix} (3)(1) + (-1)(0) & (3)(5) + (-1)(-2) \\ (2)(1) + (4)(0) & (2)(5) + (4)(-2) \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 17 \\ 2 & 2 \end{pmatrix}} \]

(b) Determinants:
\(\det(A) = (3)(4) - (-1)(2) = 12 + 2 = 14\).
\(\det(B) = (1)(-2) - (5)(0) = -2\).
Product of determinants: \(14 \times (-2) = -28\).
From \(AB\): \(\det(AB) = (3)(2) - (17)(2) = 6 - 34 = -28\).
Thus \(\det(AB) = \det(A)\det(B) = -28\). \(\checkmark\)

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(AB\) ، \(AB = \begin{pmatrix} (3)(1) + (-1)(0) & (3)(5) + (-1)(-2) \\ (2)(1) + (4)(0) & (2)(5) + (4)(-2) \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 17 \\ 2 & 2 \end{pmatrix}}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\det(AB) = \det(A)\det(B)\) ، \(\checkmark\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 - kx^2 + 5x - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(8\). What is the value of the constant \(k\)?
question.ar: عندما the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 - kx^2 + 5x - 6\) يُقسم على \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(8\). ما قيمة the constant \(k\)?

solution.en:
By the Polynomial Remainder Theorem, the remainder upon division by \(x - 2\) is equal to \(P(2)\):
\[ P(2) = 8 \]\[ 2(2^3) - k(2^2) + 5(2) - 6 = 8 \]\[ 2(8) - 4k + 10 - 6 = 8 \implies 16 - 4k + 4 = 8 \implies 20 - 4k = 8 \]\[ -4k = -12 \implies k = \mathbf{3} \]
solution.ar:
بتطبيق Polynomial Remainder Theorem, the remainder upon division by \(x - 2\) is equal to \(P(2)\):
\[ P(2) = 8 \]\[ 2(2^3) - k(2^2) + 5(2) - 6 = 8 \]\[ 2(8) - 4k + 10 - 6 = 8 \implies 16 - 4k + 4 = 8 \implies 20 - 4k = 8 \]\[ -4k = -12 \implies k = \mathbf{3} \]

question.en: Find all real solutions to the rational equation \(\dfrac{x}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{x+3} = \dfrac{5}{x^2+x-6}\).
question.ar: أوجد all real solutions to the rational equation \(\dfrac{x}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{x+3} = \dfrac{5}{x^2+x-6}\).

solution.en:
Notice that the common denominator factors as \(x^2 + x - 6 = (x - 2)(x + 3)\).
Domain restrictions: \(x eq 2\) and \(x eq -3\).
Multiply both sides by \((x - 2)(x + 3)\):
\[ x(x + 3) + (x - 2) = 5 \implies x^2 + 3x + x - 2 = 5 \]\[ x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0 \]
Apply the quadratic formula with \(a = 1, b = 4, c = -7\):
\[ x = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{4^2 - 4(1)(-7)}}{2(1)} = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{16 + 28}}{2} = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{44}}{2} = \frac{-4 \pm 2\sqrt{11}}{2} = \mathbf{-2 \pm \sqrt{11}} \]
Neither solution equals \(2\) or \(-3\), so both solutions are valid.
solution.ar:

Domain restrictions: \(x eq 2\) and \(x eq -3\).
اضرب الطرفين في \((x - 2)(x + 3)\):
\[ x(x + 3) + (x - 2) = 5 \implies x^2 + 3x + x - 2 = 5 \]\[ x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0 \]

\[ x = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{4^2 - 4(1)(-7)}}{2(1)} = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{16 + 28}}{2} = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{44}}{2} = \frac{-4 \pm 2\sqrt{11}}{2} = \mathbf{-2 \pm \sqrt{11}} \]
Neither solution equals \(2\) or \(-3\), so both solutions are valid.

question.en: In the standard \((x, y)\) coordinate plane, the lines with equations \(2x - y = 7\) and \(x + y = 5\) intersect at the point \((a, b)\). What is the value of \(a\)?
question.ar: In the standard \((x, y)\) coordinate plane, the lines with equations \(2x - y = 7\) and \(x + y = 5\) intersect عند النقطة \((a, b)\). ما قيمة \(a\)?

hints.en: The point of intersection \((a, b)\) satisfies both linear equations simultaneously: 1) \(2a - b = 7\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \((a, b)\) ، \(2a - b = 7\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: 2) \(a + b = 5\) To solve for \(a\), add the two equations together to eliminate \(b\): \((2a - b) + (a + b) = 7 + 5\) \(3a = 12\) \(a = 4\).
hints.ar: 2) \(a + b = 5\) To أوجد قيمة \(a\), add the two equations together to eliminate \(b\): \((2a - b) + (a + b) = 7 + 5\) \(3a = 12\) \(a = 4\).

hints.en: Substituting \(a = 4\) into the second equation gives \(4 + b = 5\), which yields \(b = 1\). Thus, the lines intersect at \((4, 1)\), and the value of \(a\) is \(4\).
hints.ar: Substituting \(a = 4\) into the second equation gives \(4 + b = 5\), which yields \(b = 1\). وعليه، the lines intersect at \((4, 1)\), and the value of \(a\) is \(4\).

solution.en:
The point of intersection \((a, b)\) satisfies both linear equations simultaneously:

1) \(2a - b = 7\)
2) \(a + b = 5\)

To solve for \(a\), add the two equations together to eliminate \(b\):
\[ (2a - b) + (a + b) = 7 + 5 \]
\[ 3a = 12 \]
\[ a = 4 \]

Substituting \(a = 4\) into the second equation gives \(4 + b = 5\), which yields \(b = 1\). Thus, the lines intersect at \((4, 1)\), and the value of \(a\) is \(4\).

- A common misconception is solving for \(b = 1\) and selecting 1 (Choice A).
- Another error is an arithmetic mistake in dividing 12 by 3 to get 3 (Choice B).
- Choice D represents the constant from the second equation without solving the system.
